title: Indian Market News Brief — 21 Nov 2026 — Nifty 50
quick_read: Record foreign investment and strong company profits may help Indian stocks rise. Falling crude oil prices and a stronger rupee also help lower costs for many Indian businesses. However, a stronger rupee could hurt IT company profits, and a sharp global selloff in US tech stocks creates uncertain market conditions.

stories.headline: FPIs make strong comeback, invest record ₹1.22 lakh cr in Indian equities in Nov
stories.summary: Foreign investors bought a record ₹1.22 lakh crore of Indian shares in November. This strong buying comes after heavy foreign selling between late 2024 and October 2026. The inflows helped Indian benchmark stock indexes reach nine-month highs.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Heavy buying by overseas funds brings fresh money into large Indian stocks and pushes share prices higher.

stories.headline: Sebi proposes easing disclosure rules for foreign funds
stories.summary: SEBI has proposed removing extra disclosure rules for foreign portfolio investors. The market regulator noted that these strict rules do not match global habits. The change aims to prevent foreign investors from avoiding Indian equity markets.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Simpler paperwork and easier compliance make it more appealing for foreign funds to invest in Indian stock markets.

stories.headline: Sharp rupee appreciation may cut IT firms' FY27 earnings by up to 13%: Report
stories.summary: A report indicates that a stronger rupee could cut Indian IT companies' profit earnings by up to 13% in FY27. Firms with large business in Europe face the biggest risk to their profit margins. Finding new ways to cut business costs has become harder for these companies.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: IT companies collect most of their sales in foreign money, so a stronger rupee reduces their earnings when converted back to Indian rupees.

stories.headline: India Inc. posts strongest earnings quarter since late 2023, full-year growth seen at 14%
stories.summary: India Inc delivered its best quarterly profit results since late 2023. About 67% of companies tracked by HSBC matched or beat analyst estimates. Full-year profit growth for Indian businesses is estimated at 14%.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Growing company profits give investors confidence to pay higher prices for shares.

stories.headline: BSE Sensex rejig: Shriram Finance to replace Trent; Which stocks are entering and exiting other BSE indices? Check list
stories.summary: Shriram Finance will enter the 30-stock BSE Sensex index on December 21, 2026, replacing Trent. In addition, five companies including Punjab National Bank and Havells India will exit the BSE 100 index.

stories.headline: Rupee soars to 7-month high against the dollar, strengthens below 93 level
stories.summary: The Indian rupee rose to a seven-month high against the US dollar, settling near 92.67. At the same time, crude oil prices fell for a third straight week due to steady supplies from West Asia. Government loan yields softened alongside lower oil prices.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Lower oil prices reduce import bills for India, helping lower costs for transportation, paints, and chemical companies.

stories.headline: HDFC Bank shares recover 22% in Nov, adds ₹2.38 lakh crore in market value. What's fuelling the rebound?
stories.summary: HDFC Bank shares surged 22% during November, adding ₹2.38 lakh crore to its overall value. Better quarterly performance and easing management concerns helped restore investor confidence. Despite this jump, the stock remains down 14% for the year 2026.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: HDFC Bank is a heavyweight stock in the index, so a rise in its share price directly lifts the main index.

stories.headline: Nasdaq 100 sinks 5.6% in worst week since Covid, S&P 500 corrects to 3.7% as investors sell off AI, tech stocks
stories.summary: US technology shares suffered a sharp drop as investors sold off artificial intelligence stocks. The Nasdaq 100 dropped 5.6% in its worst weekly performance since March 2020. Concerns over slow data center construction and high valuations triggered the selloff.
stories.impact: Unclear for Nifty: Weakness in global tech shares could weigh on Indian IT stocks, but global funds moving away from US tech might redirect money into Indian blue-chip shares.

stories.headline: Forex reserves decline by $14 billion to $705 billion amid valuation effects, gold price decline
stories.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves dropped by $14 billion to reach $705 billion. The Reserve Bank of India attributed the fall to a stronger US dollar and lower gold prices, which reduced the overall calculated value of the reserves.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: A drop in foreign reserves slightly reduces the central bank's reserve safety cushion to control sudden currency fluctuations.

stories.headline: RBI to conduct 4-day Variable Rate Repo (VRR) auction under LAF on November 23, 2026
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India announced a four-day short-term auction to inject ₹50,000 crore into commercial banks on November 23, 2026. This step was taken after reviewing current money conditions in the banking system.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Supplying short-term cash to commercial banks helps them handle daily business needs smoothly without facing cash shortages.
